name: Palm frond
desc: Long, tough leaves. Good for weaving.

name: Coconut
desc: Husk for fibre, shell for floats, meat for bait.

name: Driftwood
desc: Sun-bleached and dry. Burns well, floats better.

name: Stone
desc: A fist of dark volcanic rock that takes an edge.

name: Vine
desc: Green and supple. Lashes anything to anything.

name: Bamboo
desc: Light, straight and strong. Needs a knife to cut.

name: Shell
desc: Hard and bright. Grinds into a hook with patience.

name: Fish bone
desc: A clean backbone. Hooks and needles hide inside.

name: Feather
desc: A gull's flight feather. It flutters in water as it does in air.

name: Cordage
desc: Coconut fibre twisted into cord. Holds a knot.

name: Rope
desc: Ship's rope, salt-stiff but sound.

name: Canvas
desc: A torn length of sailcloth.

name: Plank
desc: A length of ship's timber with the nails still in it.

name: Sea glass
desc: A bottle shard tumbled smooth by the sea. Someone will want it.

name: Bottle
desc: Corked. Something rattles inside.

name: Waterlogged crate
desc: Ship's stores, mostly ruined. Mostly.

name: Sand flea
desc: A mole crab from the wet sand. Small fish love them.
visualNotes: It is a mole crab, Emerita, not a shrimp or a flea: a smooth, egg-shaped grey-tan shell like a large olive, seen slightly from above, with no claws and no visible legs (they tuck underneath). Only two tiny eyes on thin stalks and a pair of feathery antennae show at the front.

name: Small crab
desc: A lively little crab. Wary fish that ignore everything else eat crabs.

name: Cut bait
desc: Strips of fish. Bleeds scent into the water; predators notice.

name: Coconut meat
desc: White chunks of coconut. The little reef fish will peck at it.

name: Rusty hook
desc: Small, and more rust than steel. It came with the rod.

name: Shell hook
desc: Ground from a shell. Small and brittle, but it catches fish.

name: Bone hook
desc: A larger gorge of fish bone. Small fry cannot take it; better fish can.

name: Old rod
desc: A cracked ship's rod. Short casts, no backbone.

name: Bamboo rod
desc: A long, whippy cane. Casts to the reef edge and bends instead of breaking.
visualNotes: A castaway made it, so there is no reel, no metal line guides and no cork handle. A plain length of green-gold bamboo, longer than the old rod, with its knuckles showing, tapering to a thin tip; brown coconut-fibre cord whipped round the butt as a grip and round the tip, where a line is tied on and hangs loose.

name: Old line
desc: Sun-rotted line. Fine for small fish.

name: Braided line
desc: Three strands of cordage, braided and oiled. Strong.

name: Coconut float
desc: A disc of coconut shell. It shows a bite clearly and gives more time to strike.
visualNotes: A round disc cut from a coconut shell, its rim whole and smooth with nothing bitten out of it ('shows a bite' means it bobs when a fish takes the bait). A short wooden peg through a hole in the centre, with the line tied to the peg.

name: Stone sinker
desc: A grooved pebble. Carries the bait further and holds it on the bottom.

name: Feather lure
desc: Gull feather and shell flash on a bone hook. Wants a steady, pulsing retrieve.

name: Hammerstone
desc: A round stone that fits the hand. Makes other tools.

name: Stone knife
desc: A flake edge bound to a handle. Cuts bamboo, cleans fish.

name: Bone needle
desc: Slender and eyed. Sews what the knife cuts.

name: Campfire
desc: A ring of stones and a bed of embers that never quite goes out.

name: Drying rack
desc: Bamboo rails over a slow fire. Smoked fish keeps for the voyage.

name: Torch
desc: Split bamboo packed with husk and oil. Makes the night fishable.

name: Bait basket
desc: A lidded basket kept damp. Bait gathered into it stays lively: you find more each time.

name: Woven trap
desc: A funnel basket on a bamboo frame. Bait it, sink it, leave it.

name: Raft hull
desc: Driftwood logs under a bamboo deck.

name: Lashings
desc: Everything that holds the raft together.

name: Mast
desc: Three canes bound into one.

name: Woven sail
desc: Frond matting backed with canvas. It will hold a wind.

name: Steering oar
desc: A plank blade on a bamboo shaft.

name: Provisions
desc: Smoked fish, wrapped in leaves. Enough for the crossing.

name: Raft
desc: Driftwood, bamboo and stubbornness. It got you off the island; it will not take you much further.

name: Glass rod
desc: A second-hand fibreglass rod. Casts past the reef edge and has a backbone.

name: Graphite rod
desc: Light, stiff and long. Reaches the deep ledge and turns heavy fish.

name: Offshore rod
desc: A short, thick blue-water rod. For a bigger boat and bigger water.

name: Mono line
desc: Clear nylon. Far stronger than anything braided on a beach.

name: Heavy mono
desc: Thick nylon for fish that go for the rocks.

name: Braid
desc: Thin woven line with no stretch. Holds almost anything.

name: Spinning reel
desc: A smooth drag takes the shock out of a surge. The safe part of the gauge is wider.

name: Small steel hook
desc: Sharp and fine. For small mouths.

name: Steel hook
desc: A proper medium hook. Small fry cannot take it.

name: Large steel hook
desc: A big circle hook for big baits and big fish.

name: Shrimp
desc: Fresh shrimp from the market. Nearly everything inshore eats it.

name: Squid
desc: Tough strips of squid. Stays on the hook; reef fish like it.

name: Live sardine
desc: A lively sardine. Predators that ignore everything else will eat this.

name: Spoon
desc: A curved slip of polished metal. Flashes and wobbles. Wants to be worked fast.

name: Jig
desc: A weighted head with a tail. Hop it back slowly near the bottom.

name: Plug
desc: A painted wooden minnow that dives and swims. A steady middle pace.

name: Popper
desc: A cupped surface lure. Chug it fast and it spits water.

name: Cast net
desc: A weighted circle of mesh. Thrown over a bait school it comes back full of sardines.

name: Cooler
desc: An ice chest. The catch basket holds twelve more.

name: Crab pot
desc: A wire pot. Holds more than a woven trap and soaks longer.

name: Skiff
desc: A flat-bottomed boat with a small outboard. Reaches the mangroves, the patch reef, the Cut, and back to the island.

name: Sloop
desc: A real sea boat. Offshore water, and passages to other coasts.

name: Old coin
desc: A black disc of silver from the wreck. The market will weigh it.

name: Lantern
desc: A paraffin storm lantern. Lights the water at night as well as any torch, and does not blow out.

name: Tagging kit
desc: Dart tags, an applicator and a waterproof notebook. Protected animals you release are tagged, and Dr Reyes pays for the data.

name: Big-game rod
desc: A stand-up rod built for fish heavier than you. There is nothing in these waters it cannot hold.
visualNotes: It must look clearly different from the offshore rod, which is a blue rod with black grips and a gold lever reel. Draw no reel: the reel is a separate item. A massive stand-up rod: a short, very thick black blank with silver roller guides (small wheels instead of rings), a long curved silver aluminium butt ending in a slotted gimbal cap, and a thick white foam foregrip.

name: Big-game line
desc: Hundred-pound braid with a shock leader.

name: Lever-drag reel
desc: A two-speed reel with a drag smooth as oil. The safe part of the gauge is much wider.
